Asset type: Victoria 3 / 1776 mod commodity icon. Deliver ONE standalone square game UI asset, centered, with genuine RGBA transparency around its silhouette, never a black/white/gray background, checkerboard drawing, scene backdrop, drop-shadow rectangle or interface tile. No text, letters, numerals, logo, watermark, level badge or extra decorations. Leave safe transparent margins. It must read clearly at small game UI sizes. Create original subject artwork; reference inputs are local installed Victoria 3 assets for rendering language only, not to duplicate their subjects.
Input roles: Image 1 coal, Image 2 iron and Image 3 sulfur are STYLE references only: match their hand-painted volumetric game-object treatment, compact mass, dark crisp silhouette, restrained material highlights, soft upper-left light and simplified broad value planes. Do not copy sulfur's yellow, coal's fire glow or iron's manufactured bar shape.
Subject grounded in geology: a compact group of THREE large irregular chunks of sedimentary phosphate rock / phosphorite, with one tiny fragment. Brownish-gray to muted sand-brown, matte granular/pelletal texture and subtly layered broken faces. One medium-large central chunk, two supporting low pieces. Fine embedded darker rounded grains are understated, not gemstones. Real phosphorite is an ore containing phosphate minerals, not a pile of luminous apatite crystals. Rock shape and mid-dark brown value should distinguish it from the pale ivory rectangular limestone blocks already in this mod and bright yellow native sulfur.
Composition: large readable painted chunks occupy about 80 percent of the square; natural grounded overlap, three-quarter view. Pale warm rock-face highlights but no polished metallic specular. A simple chunky silhouette, not hundreds of gravel grains. No powder heap, bag, plant, mine, tray, scientific apparatus or frame. Transparent background.

Input roles: Image 1 mechanical tools and Image 2 academia are STYLE references only. Match painted volumetric three-dimensional objects, clear dark contour, selective realistic material highlights and readable warm/cool contrast; keep the same refined illustrative quality rather than a photograph, vector pictogram or coin.
Subject: applied mineralogy represented by a small coherent group of TWO mineral-bearing rock specimens and ONE modest historical hand magnifier. Dominant faceted gray-brown rock specimen with a clear light mineral vein crossing its broken face; smaller darker metallic ore sample beside it. The magnifier has a simple round brass rim, clear glass, short turned dark wooden handle, arranged diagonally across the right/front side to inspect the dominant mineral vein. The lens shows only a slightly enlarged portion of that same rock through the glass; not a second disconnected stone. Use period-plausible simple lens construction, inspired by museum hand-lens descriptions spanning the eighteenth/early nineteenth centuries, not a modern rubber lens or laboratory microscope.
Composition: compact isolated still life, specimens are the dominant mass, magnifier an identifiable accessory. No desk, box, textbook, labels or diagram. Distinguish this technology concept from the plain phosphate commodity pile. Soft upper-left light, neutral natural stone and patinated brass, not a monochrome golden PM. Transparent background.

Asset type: Victoria 3 production-method pictogram, NOT a goods icon or a landscape. Deliver ONE standalone square game UI asset, centered, with genuine RGBA transparency around its silhouette, never a black/white/gray background, checkerboard drawing, scene backdrop, drop-shadow rectangle or interface tile. No text, letters, numerals, logo, watermark, level badge or extra decorations. Leave safe transparent margins. It must read clearly at small game UI sizes. Create original subject artwork; reference inputs are local installed Victoria 3 assets for rendering language only, not to duplicate their subjects.
Input roles: Images 1, 2 and 3 are native PM STYLE references only. Very closely match their SIMPLE ochre/beige/patinated gold painted shallow-bas-relief language, dark brown edge contour, few broad tonal values, matte surface and understated thickness. Ignore any black appearance behind the input cutouts: output genuine alpha. Do NOT generate a glossy photorealistic miniature or detailed woodgrain machinery.
Subject grounded in historical ore dressing: ONE simple compact inclined rectangular sorting/washing sieve on short supports, with just a few large stylized rock fragments. Main sieve has a thick ochre rim and only 4 or 5 broad parallel openings suggesting a separating screen. Three coarse irregular rock shapes sit at the high end and a small clearly grouped fine/selected material cluster below the low end, showing separation. Screen seen in slight three-quarter view; a coherent primitive screen/tray rather than a modern steel factory. This is a generic UI symbol for concentration, informed by historical sieves and washing equipment, not a complete chemical process diagram.
Composition: two main visual masses, sieve apparatus and rock cluster; bold silhouette occupying 80 percent of square. Minimal geometry, no tiny bolts, planks texture, people, arrows, pipes, grinding wheel, furnace, bubble/flotation cells or water scenery. Keep the same restrained beige-gold palette as the native references. No frame or tile. Transparent background.

Asset type: Victoria 3 / 1776 mod technology icon. Deliver ONE standalone square game UI asset, centered, with genuine RGBA transparency around its silhouette, never a black/white/gray background, checkerboard drawing, scene backdrop, drop-shadow rectangle or interface tile. No text, letters, numerals, logo, watermark, level badge or extra decorations. Leave safe transparent margins. It must read clearly at small game UI sizes. Input roles: Images 1 and 2 are native technology STYLE references only, not subject references. Match richly hand-painted volumetric objects, natural material values, crisp dark contour and soft upper-left light. No fixed medallion border.
Subject grounded in historical geological surveying: ONE gently curled folded cream parchment sheet displaying a simple hand-colored geological CROSS-SECTION, and ONE small brass hinged drawing divider/compass lying diagonally along the lower/front edge. The sheet's diagram shows a gently undulating ground line above four broad contiguous gently dipping layers, subdued blue-gray, olive, ochre and warm clay-brown; this is a plausible cut through rock strata inspired conceptually by William Smith's early nineteenth-century geological sections, not a copy of any complete historical map. Layers continue beneath the surface and do not float as disconnected ribbons. No recognizable national outline, legible legend, labels, handwriting, letters, numbers or scale marks.
Composition: a compact angled page object with enough folds/rolled corner to read as paper, diagram plainly visible without filling the whole canvas like an infographic. Brass divider has two slender hinged legs and no extra gadget. Parchment dominant, accessory modest. Painted illustration, not a flat vector logo and not a terrain landscape. Transparent background.

Asset type: Victoria 3 production-method pictogram, an ACTIVE manual process. Deliver ONE standalone square game UI asset, centered, with genuine RGBA transparency around its silhouette, never a black/white/gray background, checkerboard drawing, scene backdrop, drop-shadow rectangle or interface tile. No text, letters, numerals, logo, watermark, level badge or extra decorations. Leave safe transparent margins. It must read clearly at small game UI sizes. Create original subject artwork; reference inputs are local installed Victoria 3 assets for rendering language only, not to duplicate their subjects.
Input roles: Images 1 and 2 are native PM STYLE references only. If Image 3 is supplied, it is the newly created ore-concentration PM STYLE anchor: preserve its shallow relief, palette, contour thickness and low-detail treatment. Native reference cutouts may look black behind the symbol: do not reproduce this, output alpha.
Subject grounded in historical hand sorting: ONE stylized bare hand with a short wrist entering diagonally from upper right and selecting ONE rock fragment between naturally opposed thumb and index finger, from TWO simple stones grouped below. Clear uncluttered silhouette, anatomically plausible but simplified fingers, hand/palm visible enough that this reads as hand sorting rather than a fist or glove. Total three broad ore shapes including the lifted fragment. No person's body, sleeve scene, desk or basket.
Rendering: restrained ochre/beige/patinated gold shallow painted bas-relief, dark brown contour, matte, few broad shades, no lifelike skin tones, polished gold jewelry or glossy 3D. Same visual family as concentration PM, with two main masses: hand and stones. Large compact subject about 80 percent of square. No barred machine, cancellation cross or disabled badge: Tri manuel is a method, not an off-state. Transparent background.

Asset type: ONE square Victoria 3 building icon for a phosphate mine. Output original subject illustration, not a contact sheet or a screenshot.
Input roles: Image 1 native coal mine and Image 2 native iron mine are STYLE AND FRAME references only. Match their thin rounded-corner patinated brass/bronze outer frame, slight bevel, filled hand-painted site seen from inclined three-quarter view, quiet background details and an enlarged commodity in lower right. If Image 3 is supplied, it is the original phosphate commodity DESIGN anchor: use its same brownish-gray pelletal rocks, shape language and matte material for the foreground phosphate.
Scene: an early hand-worked phosphate extraction site, a shallow excavated brown-gray sedimentary rock face/pit and a modest timber winding hoist with a rope over a wooden wheel, a small simple barrow for manual material handling. Period-plausible wood, rough masonry and hand tools; no giant modern machinery. A quieter small timber shelter behind; no tall steel headframe or smokestacks. This is an original period-adapted composite inspired by archived descriptions of manual phosphate pits, NOT a literal reconstruction of the dated Dunnellon photograph or a claim that its mine existed in 1776.
Foreground: the phosphate chunks from the design anchor occupy the lower right about one third of the icon, dominant and readable, not tiny decor and not a white metal ingot. Background mine remains subordinate but recognizable. Same muted earthy scene and strong foreground readability as the two native building references.
Important alpha rule: scene INSIDE the rounded metal frame must be fully opaque, with NO transparent holes in sky, earth or rocks. ONLY exterior corner areas outside the complete frame are genuinely transparent. Frame entirely visible, never cropped. No detached floating frame, no white/black backdrop. No text, initials, numerals, logos, watermark, extra inset medallion, modern vehicles, conveyor belts or green crystal fantasy. Square.
